answer: A museum I found genuinely fascinating was the Bangladesh National Museum in Shahbag, Dhaka, which I first visited on a school trip years ago and again more recently with my younger sister. Although it is quite a long journey from Sirajganj, both visits were well worth the effort. It houses an impressive collection spanning our country's history, from ancient artefacts to modern art, spread over several floors. What I found most [[captivating]] was the section on ancient Bengal, with terracotta plaques, stone sculptures and old coins, some of them more than a thousand years old, beautifully preserved behind glass. Walking through the galleries felt like stepping through different eras, which was genuinely [[enlightening]]. I also spent a long time in the Liberation War gallery, where there are photographs, letters and personal belongings of people who fought in 1971, and that part was very emotional. My sister was particularly interested in the paintings by Zainul Abedin, one of our most celebrated artists. I have always believed that museums are an [[underrated]] way to learn, far more vivid than any textbook. Seeing real historical objects gave me a much deeper appreciation of the past, and it made the stories my grandfather tells feel more real. The building itself was grand and well maintained, adding to the [[sense of occasion]]. Honestly, I could easily have spent an entire day there without getting bored. I think places like this are [[invaluable]], because they keep our history alive for future generations to discover and appreciate.

followUps.q: Do you often go to museums?
followUps.answer: Not as often as I would like, as there are few museums near Sirajganj. Whenever I visit Dhaka for more than a couple of days, though, I try to spend an afternoon in a museum or gallery.

I think entry should be free or very cheap, especially for students, because museums are educational. If people have to think twice about the price, the ones who would benefit most will simply stay away.

note: Named the real museum (Shahbag, Dhaka); replaced vague 'ancient civilisations' with ancient Bengal terracotta and sculpture; added the Liberation War gallery, Zainul Abedin and his sister; added mark 'sense of occasion'.
